groups.title: Dice and rolls
groups.intro: How a roll works: Characteristic + Ability + die against an Ease Factor; simple and stress dice, botches, and rounding.

entries.title: Die Rolls
entries.summary: Most actions are resolved by adding a Characteristic and an Ability to a die roll and comparing the total with an Ease Factor; the margin of success shows how well the action went. Magic uses the same basic pattern with its own totals.
quotes: the roll is normally Characteristic + Ability + Die Roll against an Ease Factor
If the total equals or exceeds the Ease Factor, the action succeeds.

entries.title: Simple Die
entries.summary: The simple die is a single ten-sided die read at face value, with a zero counting as ten. It is used when a roll carries no risk of spectacular success or failure.
quotes: Roll a ten-sided die. Each number counts for its value, except that a zero counts as ten.

entries.title: Stress Die
entries.summary: A stress die is rolled when a character is under pressure. A one is rerolled with the result multiplied up each time it repeats, and a zero on the first roll means checking botch dice to see whether the roll is a botch or simply nothing.
quotes: On a roll of one, roll again and double the number rolled.
On the first roll, zero counts as zero, and you must normally roll for a botch.
On a botch, your total for the roll is never any higher than zero, in addition to any other consequences.

entries.title: Botch Dice
entries.summary: Botch dice measure how likely a stress roll is to go disastrously wrong; the more that come up zero, the worse the outcome. The storyguide sets the number from circumstances, and a table gives the chance of a botch for each number of dice.
quotes: The base for most situations is a single botch die.
the chance of a botch can never be higher than 10%.

entries.title: Rounding
entries.summary: Where a rule involves division and does not say which way to round, the result is rounded down.
quotes: but if it does not, round down.

entries.title: Ease Factor
entries.summary: A table of standard Ease Factors from trivial to almost impossible, with notes on how likely characters of differing skill are to succeed at each. Storyguides use it to set difficulties for ordinary rolls.
quotes: Moderate skill is a score of 3 in an Ability, 'Skilled' means a score of 6, and 'Very Skilled' means 9.

entries.title: Equipment Bonuses (optional rule)
entries.summary: Optional rule letting non-essential equipment reduce the Ease Factor of an Ability roll by a minor or major amount, with only one bonus per roll and matching penalties for poor equipment.
quotes: Minor assistance subtracts 1 from the Ease Factor, whereas major assistance subtracts 3.

entries.title: Equipment Bonuses table
entries.summary: Example table of pieces of equipment, the Ability and specialty they assist, and whether the help is minor or major.

groups.title: Kinds of characters
groups.intro: Magi, companions, grogs and Mythic Companions, and who plays them.

entries.title: Character Types
entries.summary: Introduces the three kinds of player character: magi, companions and grogs. Most players keep more than one character, played according to what the saga needs.

entries.title: Companions
entries.summary: Companions are important non-magi who belong to one player. They normally lack The Gift and should be linked to another player's magus rather than to their own.
quotes: Companions should generally not have The Gift, unless you intend to play through apprenticeship so that they become magi at some point.

entries.title: Grogs
entries.summary: Grogs are minor, often shared characters, usually built from templates or detailed creation with limits: no Major Virtues or Flaws, no Story Flaws, and never The Gift.
quotes: grogs can never have The Gift

entries.title: Mythic Companions (overview)
entries.requires: Troupe approval and a Mythic Companion Virtue
entries.summary: Introduces Mythic Companions, non-Hermetic characters such as non-Hermetic wizards or supernatural warriors whose power approaches a magus's. They are normally played as an alternative to a magus, and the troupe may disallow them.

groups.title: Characteristics
groups.intro: The eight Characteristics, what each measures, and how they change.

entries.title: Characteristics
entries.summary: The eight inborn Characteristics each have a score centered on average; they are fixed apart from rare drastic events or powerful magic.
quotes: All but the most exceptional of individuals have Characteristics that fall between -3 and +3.

entries.title: Characteristic Descriptions
entries.summary: Describes what each Characteristic (Intelligence, Perception, Strength, Stamina, Presence, Communication, Dexterity and Quickness) represents and which Abilities and activities rely on it.
quotes: Spellcasting relies on Stamina.
Your effective Quickness is usually modified by your Encumbrance.

groups.title: Abilities
groups.intro: What Abilities are, their types and specialties, and each Ability in the books, from Animal Handling to Swim.

entries.title: Abilities
entries.summary: Abilities are learned skills in five types. Academic, Arcane and Martial Abilities need an appropriate Virtue or Flaw (or being a magus), Supernatural Abilities need a specific source, and Spell Mastery is for Hermetic magi only.
quotes: A character can only learn Academic, Arcane, or Martial Abilities if he has an appropriate Virtue or Flaw, or is a magus.

entries.title: Abilities Overview and Ability Rolls
entries.summary: Introduces Abilities and the basic Ability roll: add a Characteristic and an Ability to a die roll and meet or exceed an Ease Factor, with the Characteristic chosen to fit the situation.
quotes: Abilities are normally used by adding Characteristic + Ability + die roll, and meeting or exceeding an Ease Factor.

entries.title: Specializations
entries.summary: Each Ability except Spell Mastery gets a specialization that raises the effective score when the specialization applies.
quotes: you act as if your score were one level higher than it actually is

entries.title: Abilities With No Score
entries.summary: Explains whether and how a character with no score in an Ability can use it, depending on whether the Ability is asterisked and whether any experience has been put in it.
quotes: she may use it as if it had a score of zero, but rolling three extra botch dice
Characters cannot use Supernatural Abilities unless they have at least one experience point in the Ability.

entries.title: Ability Roll (summary box)
entries.summary: Summary box giving the standard Ability roll, the use of unscored Abilities and the specialization bonus.
quotes: Characteristic + Ability + die roll, meet or exceed the Ease Factor to succeed

entries.title: Ability Types
entries.summary: Lists the six types of Ability and notes that they are used alike, the difference being who may learn them.
quotes: There are six types of Ability

entries.title: General Abilities (type)
entries.summary: General Abilities can be learned by almost anyone with no game restrictions.
quotes: there are no game restrictions on who may do so

entries.title: Academic Abilities (type)
entries.summary: Academic Abilities need formal training, a Virtue or magus status for beginning characters, and usually a minimum score in a learned language.
quotes: Academic Abilities require formal training.
learning an Academic Knowledge normally requires a Latin, Greek, Hebrew, or Arabic score of at least 3

entries.title: Arcane Abilities (type)
entries.summary: Arcane Abilities may be bought at character generation only with a permitting Virtue or as a magus, and some Virtues also allow Penetration.
quotes: A character may only take these Abilities during character generation if permitted to by a Virtue, or if he is a magus.

entries.title: Martial Abilities (type)
entries.summary: Martial Abilities may be bought at character generation only with a permitting Virtue or Flaw, or as a magus.
quotes: Characters may only gain Martial Abilities during character generation if they are permitted to do so by a particular Virtue or Flaw, or if they are magi.

entries.title: Spell Mastery Abilities (type)
entries.summary: Spell Mastery Abilities belong to magi and concern casting Formulaic and Ritual spells; full rules are in the Hermetic Magic chapter.
quotes: Spell Mastery Abilities can only be taken by magi

entries.title: Supernatural Abilities (type)
entries.requires: Virtue granting the Ability, or The Gift
entries.summary: Rules for obtaining Supernatural Abilities at creation, their realm of origin and the Warping immunity that goes with it, and how The Gift lets Gifted characters learn them in play.
quotes: Characters may only gain Supernatural Abilities during character creation if they have the Virtue granting the Ability.
If you have no reason to choose otherwise, your Ability is granted by the Magic realm

entries.title: Animal Handling
entries.summary: Care and use of animals, including raising, tending, grooming, and healing them.

entries.title: Athletics
entries.summary: General physical prowess. It includes moving smoothly, confidently, and with grace.

entries.title: Awareness
entries.summary: Noticing things, be they things you are looking for or things that you are not expecting. It is also used to see how alert you are in circumstances that require watchfulness.

entries.title: Bargain
entries.summary: The know-how to get the greatest return for a service or product, while paying the least. It involves reading the person with whom you haggle, a general knowledge of the value of goods, and presenting yourself in certain ways.

entries.title: Brawl and Dodging
entries.summary: Brawl covers unarmed and improvised-weapon fighting and is the Ability used to dodge when a character has no Martial Abilities.
quotes: Brawl is also the Ability used to dodge attacks if you have no Martial Abilities.

entries.title: Carouse
entries.summary: The ability to enjoy oneself without suffering adverse effects. A person with this skill can, for example, consume prodigious amounts of alcohol without passing out.

entries.title: Charm
entries.summary: Enticing, fascinating, and endearing others to you, but only on a personal basis. It can be used to win someone over emotionally, especially romantically.

entries.title: Chirurgy
entries.summary: Medieval surgery used to help others recover from physical damage; the rules for its use are on the wound recovery page.
quotes: See page 405 for rules.

entries.title: Concentration
entries.summary: The storyguide may call for a Concentration roll before a demanding task or a retry after failure, and it helps magi hold spells through distractions.
quotes: the storyguide can call for a Concentration roll before you can make the attempt

entries.title: Etiquette
entries.summary: You know the social graces and how to behave in different situations. Etiquette differs from Charm in that Etiquette covers proper behavior, rather than charming behavior.

entries.title: Folk Ken
entries.summary: Folk Ken lets a character read another person's background and motives, with the storyguide often rolling in secret so the player does not know the result.
quotes: Often the storyguide secretly rolls a die when this Ability is used.

entries.title: Guile
entries.summary: Guile covers lying, feigning and disguise, often as an opposed roll; understanding the target gives a bonus.
quotes: roll 9+ on Perception + Folk Ken
It is often an opposed roll, against the victim's Perception + Folk Ken or, for disguise, Perception + Awareness.

entries.title: Hunt
entries.summary: Setting snares, choosing appropriate hunting spots, and following and identifying the spoor of creatures of all varieties. This Ability also lets you cover your tracks or not leave any in the first place.

entries.title: Intrigue
entries.summary: Dealing and plotting, including subtle use of power in non-confrontational ways to achieve your own ends. Intrigue need not be underhanded or manipulative — it also covers negotiations and knowledge of formal and informal rules of conduct and politeness.

entries.title: Leadership
entries.summary: Getting people to obey your orders and to follow you. Can also be used to inspire fear in others, cowing them into submission.

entries.title: Music
entries.summary: The ability to sing, play musical instruments, and compose new music.

entries.title: Ride
entries.summary: Riding and controlling a riding animal, especially under stress.

entries.title: Stealth
entries.summary: Stealth covers sneaking, hiding and following people unnoticed, the latter rolled against the other person's Perception.
quotes: which is rolled against the other person's Perception

entries.title: Survival
entries.summary: Finding food, water, shelter, a direct route, and relative safety in the wilderness (a very dangerous place in Mythic Europe). This Ability covers such mundane tasks as building a fire and cooking food without implements.

entries.title: Swim
entries.summary: The ability to propel yourself through water quickly and efficiently.

entries.title: Teaching
entries.summary: The ability to teach an Ability to someone else.

entries.title: Legerdemain
entries.summary: Sleight-of-hand Ability whose use is detected by the target rolling Perception plus Awareness, with a bonus to spot particularly delicate moves.
quotes: The target of an attempt rolls Perception + Awareness to detect your actions.

entries.title: (Area) Lore
entries.summary: Knowledge of one particular region, covenant, or even a village. It includes knowing where things are in the immediate area, local history and legends, and the centers of power in the region.

entries.title: Judaic Lore
entries.summary: Judaic Lore is the knowledge of Jewish cultural practice as opposed to strictly religious details. This includes poetry, folklore, songs, and so on.

entries.title: (Organization) Lore
entries.summary: Knowledge of the legends, history, structure, operation, and goals of the specified organization. Organizations can be as large as the Church, or as small as a local craft guild.

entries.title: Guild Lore (Ability)
entries.summary: A new Organization Lore Ability covering a guild's rules and bylaws, used for checks about guild members, other guilds and trade matters, with suggested specialties.
quotes: Guild Lore is an (Organization) Lore Ability that covers the rules and bylaws of the guild.

entries.title: Area Lore: the hinterland as a resource
entries.summary: How a character uses Area Lore to find people, resources and places in a city or its hinterland, with a penalty when searching away from where he usually lives.
quotes: Characters who spend most of their time in a city, like craftsmen, subtract 3 from Area Lore rolls to find material in the hinterland.

entries.title: Area Lore Ease Factors
entries.summary: Sidebar table of Ease Factors for Intelligence + Area Lore rolls to know about shops, roads, inns, people, laws and hidden things, grouped by difficulty.
quotes: This is also the level required to contact most hedge magicians.
A person selling a service or product that is illegal, and actively repressed.

entries.title: (Mystery Cult) Lore
entries.requires: Membership or study of a Mystery Cult
entries.summary: Cult-specific lore Ability covering rites, symbolism and signs of membership, needed for Initiation rites and some cult books; explains how experience is gained and what happens when it is learned without instruction.
quotes: In game terms, Experience points in Cult Lore are acquired like any other knowledge
A magus may build the knowledge from 0, even without instruction

entries.title: Organization Lore: Knights Templar
entries.requires: Virtue granting Templar membership (or troupe permission)
entries.summary: A new General Lore Ability covering Templar rules, personalities, provinces, tactics, sign language and ciphers. Normally only available to characters who belong to the order.
quotes: This Ability also gives the character knowledge of the Templar sign language
Specialties: personalities, history, politics, tactics, sign language, a particular region. (General)

entries.title: Living Languages
entries.summary: Language Abilities measure how well a character communicates, with the lower score of two speakers setting the quality of conversation, penalties for related languages or dialects, and a table of fluency levels.
quotes: When two people speak to each other, the lower Ability score determines how well they communicate.

entries.title: Writing Systems and Artes Liberales
entries.summary: Explains that a character's Artes Liberales score also limits how many writing systems he can read and write, lists the writing systems of Mythic Europe, and describes how new systems are learned from a source.
quotes: Each point of a character's Artes Liberales score allows him to use one writing system, defined as a separate alphabet and script as well as a separate language.

entries.title: Translation and speaking across languages
entries.summary: Rules for communicating across languages: rolls needed at low Language scores, how fluency limits use of social Abilities, and penalties to both speakers for dialect differences and related languages.
quotes: A character with a Language Ability of 2 or less needs to make Communication + Language rolls to get his point across
Unless she is fluent (Language Ability 5 or better), use of a character's social Abilities is limited by her Language score.

entries.title: Languages of the Balkans
entries.summary: Lists the language families of the Tribunal and gives penalties for a speaker of one language trying to understand a closely related one, with a worked example of how a native speaker's score applies.
quotes: Even without knowing a specific language, a character who knows a language that is closely related to another language can still potentially understand a speaker:
Penalty is to both speakers.

entries.title: Languages of Germany
entries.summary: Lists the Living Languages of Germany with their dialect specialties and gives penalties applied when speakers of related languages or dialects try to understand each other, with a worked example.
quotes: Same language, different dialects: –1 penalty to both speakers
High German vs Low German: –2 penalty to both speakers
High German vs East Norse or English: –4 penalty to both speakers

entries.title: Languages of France
entries.summary: Lists the Living Languages of France and their dialects (taken as Ability specialties), and gives comprehension penalties when speakers of related languages or dialects talk to each other, with a worked example.
quotes: –1 penalty to both speakers
–2 penalty to both speakers
–3 penalty (only –2 if Frisian dialect) to both speakers

entries.title: Languages of the Nile
entries.summary: Lists the living languages and dialects of Egypt, Nubia and Ethiopia (dialects as specialties), and gives a table of penalties applied to both speakers when related languages or dialects meet.
quotes: Mahasi is on the verge of separating into a separate language, and those who know this dialect have a larger penalty than usual when talking to speakers of the other Nubian dialects.

entries.title: Dead languages of the Nile
entries.summary: Describes the dead languages Ancient Egyptian, Demotic, Meroitic and Ge'ez, how they relate to living tongues, and their scripts.

entries.title: Sign Language and the rules of silence
entries.summary: Monastic characters may know Sign Language as an Ability, treated like a Living Language, and Benedictine houses loan out books during Lent.
quotes: Monastic characters can know the Ability: Sign Language, which is equivalent to a Living Language but not as accessible.

entries.title: Sign Language (Monastery)
entries.summary: A language Ability specific to a monastery or nunnery, with a fluency scale and defaults to the sign languages of related and unrelated houses at different penalties.
quotes: It defaults to an Ability in the language of other monasteries of the same order at –3

entries.title: Canarian dialects and silbo (whistled speech)
entries.summary: How well speakers of one Canarian dialect understand another, how silbo (whistled speech) is learned, and how magi can use silbo to extend the range of Voice-range spells.
quotes: A person skilled in any Canarian dialect can communicate with speakers of other Canarian dialects as if his Ability were two points lower.
Spells in silbo are considered to be cast in booming voice.

related.text: Ancient Magic Chapter 1: The Language of Adam (casting in other languages)

entries.title: Languages of the Theban Tribunal
entries.requires: Saga set in the Theban Tribunal
entries.summary: Lists the regional languages and dialect specialties, says Romaic and Classical Greek are separate Abilities, and gives a table of comprehension penalties between related languages.
quotes: Romaic Greek and Classical Greek are mutually intelligible, but they are separate Abilities.
Romaic Greek vs Classical Greek|-2
* Penalty applies to both speakers.

entries.title: Craft (Type)
entries.summary: A general term for countless Abilities, all dealing with handiwork of some type. In general, Craft Abilities are distinguished by the material they work with, although you may also take a Craft Ability that allows the character to work with several materials in one specific way.

entries.title: Profession (Type)
entries.summary: The ability to do a job which does not involve making something. Examples include jongleur, marshal, reeve, sailor, steward, teamster, and washerwoman.

entries.title: Profession: Preaching
entries.summary: Preaching is a Profession Ability used to sway an audience to a course of action with a Communication roll against an Ease Factor, and to teach Theology to regular listeners over a season. Covers audience size, language requirement, and failure and botch results.
quotes: Communication + Preaching + stress die vs. 12
The group can be no larger than the character's Leadership score times ten.

entries.title: Profession: Apothecary
entries.summary: Describes the Profession: Apothecary Ability for identifying, growing and preparing medicinal ingredients, and the Medicine penalty when no medicinal supplies are available.
quotes: makes all Medicine rolls at a penalty of –3

versions.title: Profession: Apothecary (Pharmacopoeians)
versions.summary: Ability for identifying and preparing medicinal ingredients. Lack of proper medicinal supplies penalizes Medicine rolls and the patient's Recovery bonus, and a skilled apothecary reduces that penalty.
quotes: makes all Medicine rolls at a penalty of –3

entries.title: Profession: Herald
entries.summary: A new Profession Ability covering knowledge of the tournament circuit, heraldic devices, colors and deeds, tournament law, and locating tournaments in an area known by Area Lore.
quotes: The Ability Profession: Herald allows a character to recognize knights by their colors and heraldic devices

entries.title: Profession: Sapper, Profession: Siege Engineer and others
entries.summary: Defines the Abilities Profession Sapper, Profession Siege Engineer and Siege Weapon, with what each covers and suggested specialities.
quotes: This Ability may not be used untrained

entries.title: Civil and Canon Law
entries.summary: Civil Law is the law of the Roman Empire. Most local legal systems are based upon it (England being the notable exception), and when a law is needed to govern international relations, Civil Law is appealed to.

entries.title: Common Law
entries.summary: Knowledge of the laws of England. There is no authority for this Ability, and it is only taught in England.

entries.title: (Dead Language)
entries.summary: This skill is similar to all other (Language) Abilities, but it is only available to educated characters. It grants the ability to speak a language which is no longer used as a native language in the areas the character has lived in.

entries.title: Islamic Law
entries.summary: This is the Muslim version of Civil & Canon Law. The major sources of Islamic Law are the Qur'an and the Sunna.

entries.title: Medicine
entries.summary: Medicine is the formal study of the body and its diseases. Medical practice is based on the theory of the four humors: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.

entries.title: Philosophiae
entries.summary: There are three philosophies natural philosophy, moral philosophy, and metaphysics. Aristotle is the auctor for all of them, in different books.

entries.title: Rabbinic Law
entries.summary: This is the Jewish version of Civil & Canon Law. The major sources of Rabbinic Law are the Talmud, the Oral Torah, and the Responsa of the Geonim.

entries.title: Theology: Christian
entries.summary: Theology is the study of God and his work in the world. The auctores are the Bible and Peter the Lombard's *Sententiae*, the Bible having theoretical primacy, being infallible, and the Sentences being most studied.

entries.title: Theology: Islam
entries.summary: This is the Islamic equivalent of Theology: Christian. The major sources for Islamic theology are the Qur'an and the Sunna.

entries.title: Theology: Judaism
entries.summary: This is the Jewish equivalent of Theology: Christian. The major sources for Jewish theology are the Torah, the Nevi'im, and the Kutuvim.

versions.title: Theology: Judaism
versions.requires: Jewish character with access to Academic Abilities
versions.summary: The Jewish equivalent of Christian Theology, with suggested specialties.
quotes: This is the Jewish equivalent of Christian Theology.

entries.title: Ars Notoria
entries.summary: You have memorized divine orations and rituals handed down from King Solomon that allow you to perform a kind of divine magic. *

entries.title: Art of Memory
entries.summary: Memory-palace technique: the number of loci depends on the score, and a Complex Memorization roll against an Ease Factor lets the scholar remember a scene or writing in exact detail; those without the Ability can try with extra botch dice.
quotes: The character has a number of loci equal to five times their score in Art of Memory.
Stress Die + Intelligence + Art of Memory vs. Ease Factor of 9 (or higher)

versions.title: The Art of Memory
versions.summary: Introduces the Art of Memory, once a Mystery Ability but now a common academic Ability that any scholar can learn or take at character creation.
quotes: It has entered common knowledge and can be learned by any scholar

versions.title: Art of Memory
versions.summary: Roll to memorize a complex scene or document perfectly, and the penalty rules for characters who lack the Ability.
quotes: Stress Die + Intelligence + Art of Memory vs. Ease Factor of 9 (or higher)

entries.title: Memorization Ease Factors
entries.summary: Table of Ease Factors for memorizing letters, conversations, rooms and buildings, with adjustments for length, technical material and substitute Abilities.
quotes: 9 (Average)
If the subject matter is highly technical add 3 or even 6 to the Ease Factor.

entries.title: Artes Liberales and Literacy
entries.summary: Artes Liberales is the foundation of academic study and also determines how many writing systems a character can read and write.
quotes: For every point in the Ability, the character can read and write one writing system

entries.title: Constructing a Memory Palace
entries.summary: Describes how a memory palace is structured, with five loci per room and a number of rooms equal to the Art of Memory score, and that memories can be deliberately forgotten.
quotes: The number of rooms in the memory palace is equal to the score in the Ability Art of Memory

entries.title: Islamic Law and Theology: Islam
entries.requires: Muslim character with access to Academic Abilities
entries.summary: Two Academic Knowledges used by Muslim characters: Islamic Law, the Muslim counterpart of Civil & Canon Law, and Theology: Islam, the counterpart of Christian Theology, each with suggested specialties.
quotes: This is the Muslim version of Civil & Canon Law.
This is the Islamic equivalent of Christian Theology.

entries.title: Code of Hermes
entries.summary: Judging events according to the Code of Hermes and the Peripheral Code. In addition to memorizing important precedents, this knowledge includes the practical side of enforcing Hermetic law — for example, knowing when to push for a vote or how to present an argument.

entries.title: Dominion Lore
entries.summary: Knowledge of the manifestations of the power of the Divine. Different from Church Lore (a kind of (Organization) Lore)) because it covers miracles rather than politics, and different from Theology because it is concerned with power rather than doctrine.

entries.title: Enigmatic Wisdom
entries.summary: The understanding that Criamon magi have of the Enigma. It is described in the Hermetic Magic chapter, on page [236](#enigmatic-wisdom-1).

entries.title: Faerie Lore
entries.summary: Familiarity with faerie powers, weaknesses, motivations, and areas.

entries.title: Faerie Magic
entries.summary: The connection to the power of the Faerie realm possessed by Merinita magi. It cannot be learned by other characters, even if they have access to Arcane Abilities.

entries.title: Heartbeast
entries.summary: The ability shared by all Bjornaer magi to take the form of their heartbeast. It is described in the Hermetic Magic chapter, on page [233](#bjornaer--the-heartbeast).

entries.title: Infernal Lore
entries.summary: An understanding and familiarity with the Infernal and its agents. Includes knowledge of demons and their habits and weaknesses, undead and their habits and weaknesses, and the power of curses.

entries.title: Magic Lore
entries.summary: Knowledge of magical creatures, areas, and traditions.

entries.title: Magic Theory
entries.summary: Arcane Ability for the technical knowledge of Hermetic magic, used chiefly in the laboratory and of little use without The Gift.
quotes: Knowledge of what magic is and how it works, used primarily in the laboratory.

entries.title: Parma Magica
entries.summary: Hermetic protection ritual that adds to Magic Resistance for a time, can be suppressed, can be extended to other people, and shields from the social penalties of other people's Gifts.
quotes: It lets you add 5 times your Parma Magica score to your Magic Resistance until the next sunrise or sunset, whichever comes first.
While a magus is protecting others, his effective Parma Magica score is reduced by 3 points

entries.title: Penetration
entries.summary: Getting your spell through the target's Magic Resistance. See page [215](#penetration-total) for full Penetration rules.

entries.title: Finesse
entries.summary: Arcane Ability for manipulating spells and performing special feats with them, such as positioning objects delicately or targeting spells.
quotes: You would use this Ability to position objects delicately or to target spells.

entries.title: Bows
entries.summary: Using bows and arrows.

entries.title: Great Weapon
entries.summary: Fighting with a weapon which requires two hands to use.

entries.title: Single Weapon
entries.summary: Fighting with a weapon used in one hand, possibly using a shield with the other. This includes lances used as intended from horseback.

entries.title: Thrown Weapon
entries.summary: Fighting at range using weapons which are thrown.

groups.title: Personality Traits
groups.intro: Traits that describe a character, when they are rolled, and how they change.

entries.title: Personality Traits
entries.summary: Short descriptors with scores that guide roleplaying; for magi and companions they are mostly memory aids, but for shared grogs they can be rolled with a stress die when unsure of a reaction.
quotes: If you do roll them, add nothing but the Personality Trait, and roll a stress die.

entries.title: Making Personality Trait Rolls
entries.summary: How to decide a character's action with a Personality Trait roll, how to treat opposed Traits and Personality Flaws, and how conflicting Traits shift the Ease Factor.
quotes: add the Personality Trait to the result of a stress die

entries.title: Personality Rolls
entries.summary: A table of suggested Ease Factors for Personality Trait rolls, with examples for Brave and Loyal and a general column for any Trait.

entries.title: Changing Personality Traits
entries.summary: Personality Traits can be changed freely by the controlling player, but only between sessions, to reflect events or exceptional rolls.
quotes: Personality Traits can only be changed by the player who controls the character, and only between game sessions.

entries.title: Personality Traits for grogs
entries.summary: Suggests troupes make greater use of Personality Trait rolls for grogs, gives the usual starting Traits (Brave and Loyal), and says a Personality Flaw can be matched with an extra Trait at a set value.
quotes: Most grogs should have a Brave and a Loyal Personality Trait.
This trait should have a value of +3 (for a Minor Flaw) or +6 (for a Major Flaw).

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.40

groups.title: Reputations
groups.intro: What others believe about a character, and how Reputations are gained and changed.

entries.title: Reputations
entries.summary: A Reputation has a score, a content and a type (Local, Ecclesiastical or Hermetic). To see whether someone has heard of a character, roll a stress die plus the Reputation against an Ease Factor set by distance; a bigger success means more is known.
quotes: A random person has heard of a character with a Reputation if a roll of a stress die plus the Reputation equals or exceeds the Ease Factor given on the table below.

entries.title: Reputation Ease Factors
entries.summary: A table of Ease Factors for being known, by Reputation type and how far away the listener is (village to country, parish to whole Church, covenant to whole Order).

entries.title: Changing Reputations
entries.summary: How noteworthy actions grant experience in a Reputation, how a bad Reputation can be supplanted by building a new one, and how multiple Reputations are rolled for.
quotes: Treat the Reputation as an Ability, and give the character one 'experience point' in it for every noteworthy action he performs.

entries.title: Academic Reputations
entries.summary: Academic Reputations are Reputations that grow like an Ability from experience points earned only through scholarly deeds, with lists of deeds that raise a Good or Bad Academic Reputation. Hermetic study gives no Academic Reputation.
quotes: Each time a character does any of the following, he gains one Academic Reputation experience point:
Stagnating gains a character 1 experience point per year.
Studying, increasing, or writing about the Hermetic Arts does not award Academic Reputation experience points

entries.title: Reputation rolls among nobles
entries.summary: Explains how players of nobles use Reputation rolls to estimate the overt traits, interests and resources of other members of the ruling class, and how a Reputation helps in dissuading enemies or in a knight's early career.
quotes: The players of nobles can estimate the overt personality traits, publicly declared interests, and obvious resources of members of their class using Reputation rolls.

entries.title: Noble Reputation
entries.summary: Adds Noble Reputation as a fourth style of Reputation alongside Local, Hermetic and Ecclesiastic, and defines who counts as part of the landed class for these Reputations.
quotes: This section extends the Reputation Table on page 19 of ArM5, providing a fourth style of Reputation to accompany Local, Hermetic, and Ecclesiastic.

entries.title: Prudhomme
entries.summary: Describes the ideal Reputation of a male noble, the prudhomme, and what a knight must be and do to be so regarded.
quotes: A man is a prudhomme if he is noble of blood, handsome, demonstrates prowess, and is of suitable character.

entries.title: Improving Noble Reputation
entries.summary: How a noble acquires a first Noble Reputation by entering feudal life and then raises it by spending seasons on notable deeds or through significant events, using the normal Ability experience table. Lists example activities and bonus experience for events like crusading or gaining a liege.
quotes: Every time a noble spends a season performing great deeds notable to other members of his class, he adds 1 Experience to his reputation.
Gaining a royal liege grants 6 experience points.

entries.title: The Advantages of Reputation
entries.summary: Explains that a strong Reputation lets other nobles judge a character's interests and intentions, so it affects their plans even when he does nothing.
quotes: A fierce Reputation is a potent envoy.

entries.title: Reputation Roll Adjustments
entries.summary: Tables of Ease Factors by distance and of modifiers for the subject's status and circumstances, used when rolling a Noble Reputation to recall what is known about another noble.
quotes: Same shire, county, or equivalent
A commoner in the service of a noble.
A vassal of the character making the roll.

entries.title: Reputation is Utterly Vital
entries.summary: Advice on how nobles use a rival's Reputation to predict willingness to fight, retreat, bargain or change sides, and how single actions change the effect of a Reputation without changing its score, illustrated with the story of William Marshal.
quotes: In neither John nor Stephen's case does the Reputation score fall.

groups.title: Confidence
groups.intro: Confidence Score and Points: spending them on rolls, and earning them.

entries.title: Confidence
entries.summary: Important characters have a Confidence Score and a pool of Confidence Points to spend, with no cap on how many points can be held.
quotes: These characters start with three Confidence Points.

entries.title: Using Confidence
entries.summary: Confidence Points can be spent after seeing a roll to boost the total, up to the character's Confidence Score per roll. Spent points are gone for good, and they cannot be used on a botch or on whole-season rolls.
quotes: A player may spend Confidence Points on most rolls to get +3 to the total per point spent.
A player may spend any number of points up to, but not exceeding, the character's Confidence Score.

entries.title: Getting New Confidence Points
entries.summary: At the end of a session the storyguide awards Confidence Points to characters who played a significant part, one for each of a list of achievements such as reaching goals, succeeding at a difficult task or good roleplaying.
quotes: Typical characters should gain two or three Confidence Points per session.

entries.title: Raising Confidence Score
entries.summary: A Confidence Score rises only through long-term events that greatly build self-reliance, using a Tytalus apprenticeship as the baseline.
quotes: A character's Confidence Score can only be increased by long-term story events which greatly increase the character's self-confidence and self-reliance.

groups.title: Virtues and Flaws
groups.intro: What Virtues and Flaws are, their types and sizes, and the rules for taking them.

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws Basics
entries.summary: How Virtues and Flaws are bought and balanced: Virtues cost points, Flaws grant them, Minor and Major sizes, the cap on Flaws for a central character, and what makes a Flaw acceptable to the troupe.
quotes: Major Virtues cost three points, while Major Flaws grant three points.
A central character may have up to ten points of Flaws, but no more than five Minor Flaws.

entries.title: Social Status Requirement
entries.summary: Every character must have a Social Status Virtue or Flaw to show how society sees them, usually limited to the society of the saga; some statuses are restricted by how society perceives the character's gender.
quotes: every character must have one of these, to represent the way that society sees them

entries.title: Virtue and Flaw Limits
entries.summary: General limits on taking Virtues and Flaws: repeats only when allowed, one Social Status, and guidelines for Story and Personality Flaws.
quotes: A Virtue or Flaw may be taken more than once only if the description explicitly allows it.
A character may not have more than one Major Personality Flaw.

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws for Grogs
entries.summary: Character-creation limits on Virtues and Flaws for grogs, including bans on Major Virtues and Flaws, Hermetic Virtues and The Gift.
quotes: You may take up to 3 points of Flaws, and an equal number of points of Virtues
You may not take Major Virtues or Flaws

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws for Companions
entries.summary: Character-creation limits on Virtues and Flaws for companions, including Minor Flaw limits and Social Status requirement.
quotes: You may take up to 10 points of Flaws, and an equal number of points of Virtues
You may not have more than 5 Minor Flaws

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws for Magi
entries.summary: Character-creation limits for magi: balanced Virtues and Flaws, at most one Major Hermetic Virtue, required Gift and Hermetic Magus status, and a free House Minor Virtue.
quotes: You must take The Gift and the Hermetic Magus Social Status Virtue
You may not have more than one Major Hermetic Virtue

entries.title: Social Status Types
entries.summary: Social Status Virtues and Flaws set a character's place in society, and some are Free and cost no points.
quotes: Some Social Status Virtues are Free, which means that they do not cost any points to buy.

entries.title: Social Statuses by Culture
entries.summary: Explains that available Social Statuses depend on culture and lists, per culture, which Free, Minor and Major Virtues and Flaws are available.
quotes: Free Virtues
Hermetic Magus

entries.title: Personality Flaws
entries.summary: Guidance on Major and Minor Personality Flaws, including how they drive stories, how often they may be ignored, and limits on how many a character takes.
quotes: A character may not have more than one Major Personality Flaw
Most characters should not have more than two Personality Flaws, Major or Minor

entries.title: Story Flaws
entries.summary: Story Flaws are external hooks that drag a character into stories; limited to one per character and must depend on something outside the character.
quotes: You should not take more than one Story Flaw, Major or Minor

entries.title: The Gift (Virtue Type)
entries.summary: Describes The Gift as a cost-free Virtue with its penalties, how it lets a character learn Supernatural Abilities and Hermetic Magic, and who should be allowed to have it.
quotes: The Gift is a special Virtue, because it has no cost.

entries.title: Hermetic Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Only characters with The Gift can take Hermetic Virtues and Flaws; a troupe may let a character with many Supernatural Virtues take Hermetic Flaws as Supernatural Flaws.
quotes: Only characters with The Gift can take these Virtues and Flaws

entries.title: Supernatural Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Supernatural Virtues and Flaws are tied to one of the four realms, which governs interaction with auras and grants immunity to Warping from a high aura of the same realm.
quotes: a character with a Supernatural Virtue or Flaw is immune to Warping caused by living in a high aura associated with the same realm

entries.title: Personality and Story Flaw Frequency
entries.summary: Advice for storyguides on limiting Major Personality and Story Flaws so that each has a chance to appear in play.

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws for Mythic Companions
entries.summary: Character-creation limits for Mythic Companions, who get extra Virtue points per Flaw point, a defining Free Virtue and a free Minor Virtue.
quotes: You make take up to 10 points of Flaws, and 2 points of Virtues for every 1 point of Flaws, for a maximum of 20 points of Virtues

entries.title: Tainted Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Tainted Virtues and Flaws are Infernal; sets limits on how many a character can take at creation and notes that granted supernatural abilities are Infernal powers.
quotes: no more than half a character's Virtues should be tainted
Supernatural abilities granted by Tainted Virtues or Flaws are always Infernal powers.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal, chapter 9

entries.title: Size
entries.summary: Every character has a Size score; adult humans are usually Size 0, and each step represents a multiplicative change in mass. Size matters more for non-human creatures.
quotes: Every three points of Size represents a ten-fold increase or decrease in mass

entries.title: Size Examples
entries.summary: Table of Size values with approximate heights, weights and example creatures, and the rule of thumb that each Size category roughly doubles weight.
quotes: Each Size category is approximately twice as heavy as the previous size category.

entries.title: What Size scores represent
entries.summary: Reference table of Size scores from tiny to huge with height, weight, comparison creature and the wound-penalty ranges for each Size.
quotes: | Size | Height | Weight | Comparison | Wound Penalties |

groups.title: The character sheet
groups.intro: How a character is written up.

entries.title: The character write-up format
entries.summary: Explains each line of the standard character write-up: Characteristics, aging and Warping, Confidence, combat, Soak, Fatigue, wound penalties, the Ability and Art notation with experience points, equipment, Encumbrance and spells known.
quotes: The format is Ability X(Z) (specialization), where X is the score in the Ability and Z is the number of experience points acquired towards the next level.
